role: external oracle for the electric near field inside a patterned layer whose curved walls are not one circle's: 3D finite-element fields of a dielectric ellipse and of two dielectric circles, which the split reconstructions and the plain Fourier sum are measured against

references.build: FEniCS (dolfin) 2019.1.0 underneath, gmsh 4.15.2 for the geometry and the mesh, MUMPS direct solve out of core; Python 3.14.10, from conda-forge

modified.description: used through its public Python API; the package itself was not changed

references.settings: Maxwell3DPeriodic on one eighth of the cell, using the exact mirror symmetries of normal incidence with E along x (the x mirror a perfect electric wall, the y mirror a perfect magnetic wall, and an even/odd split in z, two solves); second-order edge (Nedelec) elements; a perfectly matched layer above. The model of the cylinder reference with the cylinder replaced by the shape; the two circles enter as one half circle in the quarter cell, the other being its mirror image. Ellipse (E_ellipse): relative residual of the two direct solves 2.0e-10 and 1.7e-12, R = 0.052820 and T = 0.946815 from the same solution. Two circles (E_two_circles): residuals 1.2e-12 and 1.4e-12, R = 0.022449 and T = 0.977402. The stored phasors are in gyptis's time convention, the conjugate of Wavebit's; the consumer maps them as -exp(2 pi i h / wavelength) * conj(E), with h the layer thickness
references.discretization: tetrahedral meshes graded toward the walls and their rims: 32238 cells and 216320 complex unknowns per solve for the ellipse (smallest edge 3.69 nm), 34326 cells and 229648 unknowns for the two circles (3.62 nm); the product side is a Fourier truncation of the same cell

generator.command: python fem_shape.py e1_T2 e1 T2 12.25 1 for E_ellipse and python fem_shape.py cc_T2 cc T2 12.25 1 for E_two_circles; then the plane samples laid out on the 48 x 48 grid

cost.note: both runs, two solves each, factorization out of core, on a machine that ran other work at the same time

shapes.E_ellipse: one ellipse at the cell centre, semi-axes 130 nm along x and 80 nm along y
shapes.E_two_circles: two circles of radius 60 nm centred at (-90, 0) and (90, 0) nm from the cell centre

samples.plane: mid-height of the layer, z = 75 nm above its lower face
samples.layout: E_ellipse[j, i, component] and E_two_circles[j, i, component] at (x[i], y[j]), components (Ex, Ey, Ez)

inputs.mesh_level: T2, the second of the ladder; the first is the self-check

outcomes.reference_self_check: the next coarser mesh level differs from this one, over the same 2304 samples, by 0.38% of the plane RMS of the in-plane field for the ellipse (19478 cells; R 0.052843 against 0.052820) and by 0.38% for the two circles (20532 cells; R 0.022438 against 0.022449). The same script and environment on the cylinder of golden_gyptis_cylinder_field, at its coarsest stored level, are 0.15% from that stored level and 0.16% from the stored finest one. An FDTD solution (Meep 1.35.0, 5 nm cells) agrees with the coarser level to 0.29% of the plane RMS 15 nm or more from the walls on both cells
outcomes.failed_or_discarded: the first run of the ellipse was discarded: two faces of the x mirror were missed by a bounding-box search and carried no boundary condition, and its R + T was 1.051. The search was widened and the faces found are now checked by area; the stored run has R + T = 0.9996
